speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; can you tell me exactly how long each episode lasts and if you have any recollection of them?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status (Non-Convulsive Status Epilepticus).

The patient's presentation of recurrent staring spells lasting 3–4 minutes, post-ictal confusion, and lack of recall is highly suggestive of absence seizures that have evolved into a continuous state. The "muddy taste" likely represents an aura or gustatory hallucination associated with the seizures.

I am not requesting further tests as the clinical history is sufficient for this diagnosis; however, an EEG would be the gold standard confirmation if available.
